basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment is characteristic; skeletal, cardiac and renal malformations vary with duplication extent and lack established frequencies here.
Disorder of the sclera; the umbrella includes inflammatory and non-inflammatory conditions, so an immune mechanism is not universal.
Inherited macular degeneration with impaired visual acuity; macular disease in 4/4 patients.
Isolated vaginal developmental malformation; reproductive anatomy has no axis.
Limb reduction and renal malformations define the syndrome; pleural effusion, chylothorax and respiratory failure are annotated at 80-99%. Ear function impairment is unestablished.
Adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma, commonly arising in deep connective tissues; no specific cutaneous origin or common secondary organ occupation is established.
Non-inflammatory arthropathy and skeletal deformities dominate; pericarditis and valve disease occur in 5-29%, despite pericarditis appearing in the syndrome name.
Carcinoma originates in paranasal sinus mucosa, within the airway axis; recurrence or metastatic potential does not establish another organ label.
Renal amyloid causes progressive functional loss; frequent hepatic and pulmonary deposits do not establish impairment. Elevated liver enzymes occur in only 5-29%.
Brain malformations and hydrocephalus define the disorder, present in 13/13; polydactyly occurs in only 2/13. Other organ abnormalities lack qualifying frequencies.
Renal and intestinal amino-acid transport defects define it; neurologic dysfunction including ataxia is annotated at 80-99%. Photosensitive dermatitis is omitted under the four-axis cap.
Isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction in 3/3; the PSEN1 gene does not establish neurologic involvement.
Delirium is a disorder of cerebral attention and cognition, explicitly included in the neurologic axis.
Wasting of pelvic floor skeletal muscle is a musculoskeletal abnormality, despite placement under genital prolapse.
Porphyrin metabolic encephalopathy; cataracts in 2/3, anemia in 1/3 and splenomegaly in 2/3 support additional axes. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Inherited erythroid disorder with refractory sideroblastic anemia in 20/20; leukemia susceptibility alone does not establish secondary organ involvement.
Autoimmune thyroid disease defines the syndrome; gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic anemia are syndromic components annotated at 30-79%. Skin disease occurs in 5-29%.
Degeneration of the vitreoretinal structures; the supplied ancestry identifies a retinal disorder.
Inherited prion disease causes cerebral degeneration and cognitive impairment; prion disease is classified within transmissible CNS disease.
True skeletal muscle hypertrophy is the defining abnormality; no supported involvement of another organ axis.
Umbrella disorder defined by skeletal system involvement; specialized sites in individual subtypes do not apply across the group.
Tuberculous infection outside the lungs; anatomical sites vary across subtypes, with no single additional organ established for most patients.
GOT2 deficiency causes metabolic encephalopathy; hyperlactatemia and hyperammonemia occur in 4/4. Recurrent infections alone do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
Skin basal cell carcinoma with squamous differentiation; metastatic potential does not establish common secondary organ damage.
Lymphatic parasitic infection with chronic skin/subcutis elephantiasis; hyperkeratosis occurs in 30-79%. Renal and pulmonary disease occur in 5-29%; eyelid disease is not universal.
